industry: Screen printing, embroidery, and custom apparel shop
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Marisol will confidently state a price, deadline, or policy, then reverse herself moments later without acknowledging she's changed anything ('okay so it's $8 a shirt — wait no actually let's say $9, or maybe do $8.50, ugh let me just think'). She often flip-flops between two options mid-sentence, changes her mind about turnaround times, minimum orders, and even whether she can do a job at all. She's not trying to mislead anyone — she's genuinely torn between wanting to please customers and protecting her margins — but customers often need to get her final answer in writing or ask her to just pick one.
background_facts: Vega Ink Custom Apparel is a small print shop in Corpus Christi, Texas, run by Marisol Vega (34) with two part-time employees: Junior (screen printing) and Ashley (embroidery/heat press, only works Tues/Thurs/Sat). Shop hours: Mon-Fri 10am-6pm, Sat 11am-3pm, closed Sun. Services: screen printing (1-color from $7/shirt at 24pc minimum, but Marisol frequently quotes 12pc minimum too and isn't sure which she actually wants to enforce), multi-color printing (+$1.50 per extra color), embroidery ($12-$18/item depending on stitch count, she's genuinely unsure how to price small logos under 5,000 stitches consistently), heat-transfer vinyl for small orders under 12 pieces ($10/shirt flat, sometimes she says $12), and rush orders (she says 'usually' 50% upcharge but has waived it for friends and regulars more than once). Standard turnaround is 7-10 business days, but she often promises 5 days to close a sale and then has to walk it back. Deposit policy: 50% down to start any order over $150, though she sometimes accepts verbal agreements from repeat customers with no deposit at all, which has burned her twice (customers vanished after art proofs). Blank shirt suppliers: SanMar and Bella+Canvas, restocked bi-weekly — she's unsure whether her new supplier discount will actually lower her per-shirt cost or not, waiting on updated pricing sheet. Big pain point: she hates saying no to people so she overpromises capacity around back-to-school (August) and holiday season (Nov-Dec), leading to missed deadlines. Budget for a new website/online store is 'maybe $1,500, maybe $3,000' — she keeps going back and forth on whether to hire a freelancer or use Shopify herself. Payment accepted: Cash, Venmo, card (3% fee added, though she sometimes forgets to charge it). Popular clients: local little league teams, a few food trucks, a church youth group. She wants to add DTF (direct-to-film) printing but hasn't decided if it's this year or next year.
